mistakes: Doing a big side-to-side wave in front of the chest instead of the salute-from-forehead (a wave is understood, but it is not the dictionary sign).
Military-style salute with the palm down or starting at the centre of the forehead.
variants: Thumb may be folded in the palm (B) or open/alongside (open-B) - Handspeak.
Everyday wave: Lifeprint says HI/HELLO is often just a natural sideways wave of the hand.

mistakes: Confusing it with GOOD: THANK-YOU is aimed out toward the person; GOOD drops more downward (and can land on the other palm).
Blowing a kiss (puckering, starting on the lips with a kiss) or moving the hand back toward yourself.
THANK-YOU.nonManual: Smile (Lifeprint: 'so they'll know you mean it').
variants: Two hands (both flat hands from the chin) = 'thank you very much' / many thanks (Handspeak, Lifeprint).

mistakes: Using a fist - that makes SORRY.
Using both hands - that means ENJOY/APPRECIATE (Lifeprint).
PLEASE.nonManual: Pleading/hopeful face; Lifeprint notes a strong 'pleeease' uses head lowered, pout, and extended repetition.

mistakes: Using a flat hand - that is PLEASE.
Using a tight S-fist: Lifeprint says S is seen but less common; Handspeak calls the fist version incorrect.
SORRY.nonManual: Sorry/apologetic face (brows drawn up/together, slight frown); intensity of movement and face grade the meaning ('very sorry').
variants: S-handshape version (seen, less common).

mistakes: Moving the whole arm (knocking) instead of bending at the wrist.
Using a thumbs-up.
Using only the index finger, or wagging a finger.
Forgetting the negative head-shake.
NO.nonManual: Negative head-shake (Lifeprint: double motion + small head-shake is the 'normal' form).
variants: Single forceful snap = firm 'NO!' (Lifeprint).
Three small gentle snaps with a caring face = gentle 'no, no, no' as to a baby (Lifeprint).

mistakes: Clapping flat hands or tapping one hand into the other palm (common baby-sign distortion).
Using rounded O-hands with a hole instead of flat-O.
Tapping the chin or cheek (cheek-to-cheek is HOME).
Opening the mouth / using a round O or a fist.
Using a Y-hand (that means drinking alcohol - Lifeprint).
Tipping a thumb toward the mouth (a gesture, not the sign).
variants: Double movement (Handspeak 2nd video).
Exaggerated/held = chug/drink-up (Lifeprint).

mistakes: Making a big open/close with a spread 5-hand.
Tapping or moving the arm.
Using the ASL number 3 (thumb-index-middle) instead of W.
Palm facing forward, or tapping the cheek.
Waving the hands side to side (looks like a 'no/wave off' gesture).
Using it to mean 'finish the task' - Lifeprint: FINISH means done/already; for 'complete it' use other signs (END/PROCEED).
FINISH.nonManual: Neutral; for 'Cut it out!' use an intense face.
variants: Baby-sign teaching (Signing Time 'all done'): start with palms UP and turn the hands down and away.
One hand with a strong single movement + intense face = 'Stop it! / Cut it out!' (Lifeprint).

mistakes: Repeating the movement: Signing Time warns a repeated version means something else (not child-appropriate). Do it ONCE; show 'very hungry' with your face.
Starting at the stomach, or using a flat hand.
Touching the forehead (that is FATHER).
Using a Y- or A-hand, or touching with the fingertips.
variants: Single touch (Lifeprint: 'the most basic form is to just touch').
Fingers wiggle with thumb on chin.

mistakes: Touching the chin (that is MOTHER).
Handspeak notes that tapping the exact middle of the forehead is a mispronunciation in formal citation (fine in casual signing).
variants: Single touch or near-touch is fine (Lifeprint).
Fingers wiggle ('papa' feel; not a firm distinction).

mistakes: Arms not stacked (hands far apart) or palms facing the body.
Huge swinging movement.
Using flat or C hands (those make CLASS/GROUP).
Drawing the circle vertically.
Linking little fingers ('pinky promise').
Only one hook without the switch.
variants: Lifeprint: interlock twice (hook, switch).

mistakes: Palm facing yourself (Handspeak: 'palm outward, not inward!').
Tucking the thumb (that is the 'horns' gesture).
Using ILY for 'love' in general sentences - ILY means 'I love you' only.
Using KISS-FIST ('love it') for people - Handspeak: that version is for things/activities.
variants: Flat hands crossed over the chest.
Signing Time adds a small side-to-side rock (hug).

mistakes: Rubbing in place like PLEASE instead of brushing upward.
Blank face - show the emotion.
HAPPY.nonManual: Happy face/smile (Lifeprint: 'you've got to use your face!').
variants: Two hands (e.g., in 'Happy Birthday').

mistakes: No facial expression.
Wiggling fingers (like tears) - a gesture, not the sign.
SAD.nonManual: Sad face; head tilts forward slightly (Lifeprint).
variants: One-handed in informal register (Handspeak).

mistakes: Sliding the hands down the chest.
Confusing it with ANIMAL (rocking movement) or HAVE (no droop).
TIRED.nonManual: Tired/droopy face, shoulders slump; exaggerate for EXHAUSTED.

mistakes: Using H-hands (Lifeprint: that is Signed English, not ASL).
No facial expression - the face shows how much it hurts.
HURT.nonManual: Pained face; intensity scales with pain.
variants: Twist version: index fingers twist in opposite directions (Handspeak default; Lifeprint 'injured').
Lexicalized fingerspelling #HURT at the painful spot.

mistakes: Confusing it with THANK-YOU (THANK-YOU is aimed toward the person; GOOD drops more downward).
Flipping the palm down (that is BAD).
variants: Two-handed: dominant hand lands in the non-dominant upturned palm (Lifeprint: used for emphasis/answers; Handspeak: rarely used).

mistakes: Forgetting to flip the palm down (looks like GOOD).
Smiling while signing it.
variants: Two-handed version (Lifeprint).

mistakes: Fanning the face (a gesture).
Slow movement - the faster/stronger, the hotter (Lifeprint).
HOT.nonManual: 'Hot' face; Signing Time: open mouth and exhale as if something is hot.
variants: Signing Time teaches it with a C-shaped hand.
Handspeak variant: open-8 middle fingertip at the mouth, swipe away.

mistakes: Big slow movements.
Using it to mean 'a cold' (illness) - it only means temperature (Lifeprint).
COLD.nonManual: Hunched shoulders, tense/shivering face; faster and tighter = very cold.

mistakes: Fist under the palm (upside down).
Flat hand on flat hand.
HELP.nonManual: Raised brows when offering/asking ('Do you want help?').
variants: Tap version: the fist taps the palm twice (Handspeak; ASL-LEX codes HELP as repeated).
S-hand instead of open-A (seen; Lifeprint does not recommend).

mistakes: Closing into a fist/S instead of flat-O (Lifeprint).
Moving the hand all the way down the chest.
SLEEP.nonManual: Eyes close/droop as the hand closes (Signing Time).

mistakes: Upward thrusts with the hands leaving the body (that is ADDRESS/LIVE - Lifeprint).
Circling instead of up-and-down.
Shaking a B-hand (Lifeprint: not used by the Deaf community).
Holding a still T (that is just the letter).
BATHROOM.nonManual: To ask 'Do you need to go to the bathroom?': raise eyebrows and tilt the head forward (Lifeprint).
variants: Twist instead of side-to-side shake (Lifeprint, Signing Time).
RESTROOM (R-hands) considered more polite by some older signers (Lifeprint).

mistakes: Swapping by moving whole arms around each other (that is EXCHANGE).
Using flat hands.
variants: Dominant A-hand with non-dominant X (Handspeak variant).
Larger movement = big change.

mistakes: Doing it in front of the chest.
Using the whole hand (all fingers) to pinch.
Initializing with P-hands (Lifeprint: don't).
Moving the whole arms instead of the wrists.
Hinging on the thumb sides.
Opening and closing many times.
Snapping with the index finger (Lifeprint: always the middle finger).
Barking or tongue gestures instead of the sign.
variants: Pat the thigh with a flat hand (1-2 times), optionally then snap - very common with babies/children (Signing Time, Lifeprint, Handspeak).
Lifeprint lists 5 versions: snap x2, snap x1, pat thigh x2, snap+pat, pat+snap.

mistakes: Pulling downward instead of sideways.
Using all fingers.
variants: Two-handed (both sides of the face).
G-handshape or 8-handshape versions (Lifeprint, ASL-LEX cat_2/cat_3).

mistakes: Touching the mouth itself (that is EAT).
Only one touch in isolation (single-contact form appears in compounds like HOMEWORK).
variants: Ear-to-mouth direction (Lifeprint).

mistakes: Circling both hands in the same phase.
Using flat hands.
variants: Forward circling also used (Lifeprint: 'pick a direction and stick with it').
Quick open-and-close version for skilled signing (Lifeprint).

mistakes: Pointing with the index finger (that is ME/I).
Palm facing out.
variants: Two gentle pats = MINE (Lifeprint).

mistakes: Pointing with the index finger (that is YOU).
Palm up.
variants: Sweep across several people = YOUR (plural) (Handspeak).

mistakes: Using a flat palm (that is YOUR).
Using a flat hand (that is MY).
Tapping flat hands or palms together.
Single tap - Lifeprint: a single movement tends to mean the verb 'named/called'.
NAME.nonManual: In 'What's your name?' (YOUR NAME? / NAME YOU?) use furrowed brows and a forward head tilt (Lifeprint).

mistakes: Raising the eyebrows (that marks a yes/no question).
Asking with the hands but a neutral face.
WHAT.nonManual: WH-question face: eyebrows lowered/furrowed, head tilted slightly forward, shoulders may hunch (Lifeprint).
variants: Index finger brushes down across the non-dominant palm (older; still used; Lifeprint/Handspeak).
Lexicalized fingerspelling #WHAT (Handspeak).

mistakes: Using a D-handshape (Lifeprint: use 1).
Bending the finger instead of moving the wrist; raising the eyebrows.
WHERE.nonManual: WH-question face: eyebrows down (Lifeprint: 'They are part of the sign').

mistakes: Using the WH face for the friendly greeting HOW-ARE-YOU (see that entry).
Separating the hands before rolling.
HOW.nonManual: WH-question face (lowered brows) for a real 'how' question.
variants: Handspeak's main form uses more closed '10'-like hands twisting against each other.
One hand rolling forward (Lifeprint).

mistakes: Flicking the thumb or the whole hand.
Doing it in front of the chest.
UNDERSTAND.nonManual: Nod for 'understand'; negative head-shake for DON'T-UNDERSTAND (Lifeprint).

mistakes: Slapping the whole palm down.
Touching the back of the base hand.
Closing into fists (grabbing).
Palms down - flipping palms down is DON'T-WANT (Lifeprint).
Holding up a palm like a traffic officer (a gesture, not the ASL sign).
For 'stop it! / cut it out!' ASL uses a one-handed FINISH instead (Lifeprint).
variants: STOP+ / STOP++ repeated for commands/stress (Handspeak).

mistakes: Holding up a single index finger ('one minute' gesture).
Wiggling only one finger.
Sliding back and forth repeatedly (a double movement means 'clean up').
Tapping the fingertips together (Lifeprint: they don't touch).
Using D-hands (Lifeprint: use 1).
Tapping the chin (that is MOTHER).
Using a thumbs-up.
variants: Single touch.
Thumb on chest then move out/forward in a small arc (Lifeprint, Handspeak).

mistakes: Grabbing the bicep (Lifeprint).
Making it very large (large = ALL-MORNING).
variants: One-handed in GOOD-MORNING when the other hand is busy (Lifeprint).

mistakes: Palm up on the dominant hand.
Moving along the arm (that means EVERY-NIGHT - Lifeprint).
Doing two full, separate signs with a pause (fine for beginners, but the compound is smoother).
Forgetting the base arm in MORNING.
variants: Signing Time teaches full GOOD (landing on the other palm) + MORNING.
One-handed MORNING when holding something (Lifeprint).

mistakes: Signing GOOD + SLEEP instead (means something else).
variants: Separate full signs GOOD NIGHT = 'I had a good night' (Lifeprint).

mistakes: Adding a sign for 'to' (ASL drops it).
Signing DATE instead of MEET (Lifeprint notes this common slip).
variants: me-MEET-you (directional MEET) can replace MEET + YOU.

mistakes: Using lowered WH-question eyebrows for a casual greeting (that turns it into a serious 'how are you really?').
HOW-ARE-YOU.nonManual: Casual greeting: raised eyebrows or at least a friendly face (Lifeprint: exception to the lowered-brow WH rule). Concerned inquiry: lowered brows.
variants: Common reply: FINE (thumb of 5-hand taps chest).

mistakes: Fingerspelling 'change'.
